title: common/pkg/cgroups: add CreateFirst
body:
Podman needs to create a container's cgroup before calling the OCI runtime in rootless cgroupfs mode, so the runtime can't silently fall back to running without one
 (https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/XXXX). Podman has a couple of candidate locations, so this adds a helper that tries them in order:

   ```go
   func CreateFirst(paths []string, resources *cgroups.Resources) (string, func() error, error)
   ```

   It returns the first path that could be created and set up with `fs2.CreateCgroupPath`, plus a cleanup function for the caller to use if container creation fails later.

   The cleanup only removes a cgroup that this call actually created (decided by whether our `mkdir` succeeded, not by checking beforehand), and only with `rmdir`, so it never
 touches a cgroup that already existed or has processes in it. An existing cgroup directory is still accepted, just without a cleanup function. If cleanup of a failed candidate
 fails, it stops and returns the error instead of trying the next one.

   Which paths to try is left to the caller.

   Tested with three new tests in `cgroups_linux_test.go`. Two of them create real cgroups, so when rootless they are skipped unless `CGROUP_TEST_ROOTLESS=1` is set (meant for an
 isolated, writable cgroup namespace). I ran all three that way and they passed.

   The Podman side is in https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/pull/30079.
